art.subject: Claudia's Leaf Warbler (Phylloscopus claudiae), adult (sexes alike) in spring: a pale greyish-green median crown stripe between dark greyish-olive lateral crown stripes that are darkest towards the nape; a long yellowish-white supercilium; a dark eye-stripe; upperparts greyish-green; wings with two clear pale yellowish wing-bars; underparts whitish with a faint yellow wash; outer tail feathers with white on the inner webs; bill with dark upper mandible and pale yellowish-orange lower mandible; dark eye.
art.pose: clinging to the side of a tree trunk, side view, wings partly flicked
art.scene: mixed woodland on a Korean offshore island during spring migration in May, dappled light; no people, buildings or text
art.build: A small, compact leaf warbler, smaller than a sparrow and a little smaller than an Eastern Crowned Warbler, with a fairly large head. Bill fine and pointed, shorter than the head. Legs slender. Tail short and square. Habitually flicks its wings alternately, one after the other, and often clings to tree trunks and the undersides of branches like a nuthatch.
avoid: Do not paint a single wing-bar with a yellow vent contrasting with a white belly; that is Eastern Crowned Warbler (Phylloscopus coronatus).
Do not paint a bright lemon crown stripe or a yellow rump band (Pallas's Leaf Warbler).
Do not make the lateral crown stripes black; they are dark greyish-olive.
Do not paint bright yellow underparts.
